case_title: Fainul Khan v. State of Jharkhand and Another
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity: raised by the defence as ground for false implication; the court held the enmity irrelevant
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured witnesses P.W.7 and P.W.8); injury reports; testimony of the officer-in-charge (P.W.11)
aggravating_circumstances: Unlawful assembly; some members armed with spears; deceased surrounded to prevent escape
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302/149 (life imprisonment), s.323/149 and s.147 (varied terms), sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Not stated (High Court of Jharkhand judgment dated 28.05.2009; outcome not described in this judgment)
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 read with s.149 (murder); IPC s.323 read with s.149 (hurt); IPC s.147
neutral_facts: On the evening of 1 November 1983, a group of men armed with spears and lathis surrounded the victim and another man who were walking together. The accused surrounded both men, and one accused struck the victim on the head with a lathi. The victim fell to the ground, and when he tried to stand up, he was struck by two accused with spears. The victim later died. The second man, an injured eyewitness, was struck on the face, head and hand with a lathi by one accused. A resident of the locality, also an injured eyewitness, was struck on the head by one accused and on the thigh by another during the same incident. A further witness said he reached the scene only after hearing the commotion, when the victim was already lying on the ground. Both injured witnesses said they were taken to hospital with the victim, where their injuries were examined. One injured witness showed scars from his injuries while testifying. The officer-in-charge of the police station testified that he requested the injury reports of the witnesses, which were then made available to him before he filed the charge sheet. The first information report was lodged by the second injured witness at the hospital.
physical_harm: Death of the victim after assault with lathis and spears; injuries to P.W.7 (head, right hand, thigh) and P.W.8 (face, head, hand)
key_evidence_accepted: Ocular evidence of injured eyewitnesses P.W.7 and P.W.8; evidence of P.W.11 (officer-in-charge) on injury reports and charge sheet; scars noticed by the trial judge
witness_credibility: Injured eyewitnesses P.W.7 and P.W.8 found credible; no lacunae in P.W.8's evidence; P.W.6 not accepted as an eyewitness; P.W.11 not discredited in cross-examination
bail_history: Appellants were on bail; bail bonds cancelled and they were directed to surrender to serve the remaining sentence
trial_duration: offence: 01.11.1983; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 28.05.2009; Supreme Court: 04.10.2019
legal_representation: Accused: Sidharth Luthra, Sr. Adv. with others. State: Anil K. Jha with others
investigation_status: FIR lodged by P.W.8 at hospital; injury reports obtained on request; charge sheet filed; trial held
procedural_irregularity: Section 147 charge framed against only four of the accused (held inadvertent, no prejudice); s.313 questions alleged to be casual and perfunctory (held no prejudice)
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302/149, 323/149, 147 IPC. High Court: judgment dated 28.05.2009 (outcome not stated). Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: No lacunae in s.313 examination; no prejudice shown; objection cannot be raised at belated stage (relying on Shobhit Chamar and Fahim Khan)
defence_argument: Charge defective without ss.141/146; s.313 questioning casual and caused prejudice; injury and witness inconsistencies; no common object; alternatively liable for a lesser offence (Najabhai)
legal_principle_applied: Prejudice under s.313 Cr.P.C. must be shown on the facts, considering other evidence and questions; objection first raised on appeal requires demonstrated prejudice; s.464 Cr.P.C. failure-of-justice test for charge defects
precedent_relied_upon: Suresh Chandra Bahri v. State of Bihar 1995 Suppl (1) SCC 80; Shobhit Chamar v. State of Bihar (1998) 3 SCC 455; Fahim Khan v. State of Bihar (2011) 13 SCC 142; Sukha v. State of Rajasthan [1956] SCR 288
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds cancelled; appellants directed to surrender forthwith to serve the remaining sentence
